scenario.description: A utilization review physician must determine whether a patient in the emergency department should be admitted as an inpatient to telemetry or remain in observation, and must finalize the expected stay and follow-up plan with input from the attending physician, utilization review specialist, and patient educator.

shared_context.S1: A patient in the emergency department is being considered for either inpatient admission to a telemetry bed or continued care in the observation unit.
shared_context.S2: Dr. Singh makes the final admission-status and care-plan decision.
shared_context.S3: The patient has had intermittent palpitations and is currently receiving evaluation and treatment in the emergency department.
shared_context.S4: Before the status is finalized, Dr. Singh follows the department's routine practice of checking with the attending physician, utilization review, and patient education for any relevant information.

PF1.text: The patient's rhythm strip showed intermittent pauses that Dr. Alvarez considers unsafe without continuous telemetry for the next 24 hours; the finding is in the attending's working notes but has not yet been entered into the shared chart.

PF2.text: The patient's payer applies its two-midnight inpatient rule when the treating physician expects hospital-level treatment to span at least two midnights; the utilization review portal confirms that this case qualifies for inpatient status if that expected stay is documented.

PF3.text: The patient's daughter can attend discharge teaching only on Friday from 16:30 to 17:00, and the family has asked that the appointment be reserved in that exact window; Jon received the request by phone but has not entered it in the education schedule.

acceptance_conditions: The patient must be admitted as an inpatient.
The patient must be assigned to telemetry.
The expected stay must be documented as two midnights.
A discharge-teaching appointment with the daughter must be reserved for Friday from 16:30 to 17:00.
The telemetry-relevant rhythm finding must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C4: any(('Friday' in c['detail'] and '16:30' in c['detail'] and '17:00' in c['detail'] and ('discharge teaching' in c['detail'] or c['type'] == 'discharge_teaching' or c['type'] == 'patient_education_scheduling') and (c['target'] == 'Jon' or c['target'] == 'patient_education' or c['target'] == "patient's daughter" or c['target'] == 'patient education')) for c in commitments)

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The undocumented rhythm pauses change the admitting service from an open choice to telemetry for exactly the next 24 hours, and they provide the clinical fact that must be cited.
The payer portal's two-midnight rule changes the status to inpatient and fixes the documented expected stay at exactly two midnights instead of observation or an unspecified duration.
The daughter's availability changes the follow-up plan from an unspecified teaching arrangement to a discharge-teaching commitment reserving Friday from exactly 16:30 to 17:00.
